properties.digitized_from: OpenStreetMap (way 853562207, leisure=park, operator=Port of San Francisco, wikidata=Q108550863) -- a real, community-surveyed park boundary, not a diagram trace.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-17 (user-prompted site-completeness check): while confirming this map covers the full extent of the Pier 70 D4D, found that Figure 6.4.2 (the diagram this whole Pier 70 layer is built from) only depicts Brookfield's 28-acre leased parcel -- one of four components of the Port's 69-acre Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan (the others being Orton Development's ~5-acre historic core, already fully covered by this project's Building 101/102/104/113-116/2/12/14/21 features; Crane Cove Park itself, ~8 acres; and BAE Systems' ~28-acre active ship-repair yard/dry docks, left out of this map as continuing industrial use with no development status to track, the same reasoning already applied to Potrero's PG&E Switchyard). Crane Cove Park was never on Figure 6.4.2 at all since it's a separate, Port-led public capital project (funded by 2008/2012 Parks Bonds + grants, opened 2020) rather than part of Brookfield's D4D. Fetched its real boundary from OpenStreetMap (Overpass API, name~'Crane Cove', tagged leisure=park / operator=Port of San Francisco / wikidata=Q108550863 -- confirms this is the right feature, not a guess) rather than hand-tracing or estimating a bounding box. Real, closed-ring polygon, 34 vertices, ~6.26 acres (OSM's own traced boundary; public sources cite 7-8 acres for the overall park including areas like the boat launch/beach this specific way may not fully enclose -- treating the smaller OSM figure as what's confirmed rather than inflating to match the citation). 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: (a) Figure 6.4.2 does not depict only Brookfield's 28-acre leased parcel: it also covers Parcels K North and K South and the Hoedown Yard, i.e. the roughly 35-acre Pier 70 Special Use District (Port Item 11A p.2); Crane Cove Park is not on it, which is correct. (b) The four-component breakdown of the '69-acre' Preferred Master Plan above (Brookfield 28 acres, Orton ~5 acres, Crane Cove ~8 acres, BAE ~28 acres) is not stated on the cited Port page; the sources read support only the park's funding by the 2008 and 2012 Parks Bonds plus grants, its 2020 opening, and about eight acres for the park site (Port Item 12B, Sept 2018). The Port's 2018 news release and The Real Deal list five components (adding the 7-acre Illinois Parcels), the Port's 2019 update calls the whole area 65 acres, and the OHP 2023 sheet calls the historic core site 'seven-acre'; the ~5 and ~28 acre figures have no source read. (c) The Port's park page gives about 7 acres, so the '~8 acres' above is the 2018 report's figure for the project site.
properties.accuracy_caveat: HIGH CONFIDENCE -- real, community-surveyed OSM polygon (not a hand trace or estimate), independently confirmed via its own leisure=park/operator/wikidata tags. Its area (~6.26 acres) is somewhat smaller than the ~7 acres given on the Port's project page (the Port's 2018 Item 12B calls it an 'approximately eight acre site') -- likely because this specific traced way covers the core landscaped park and not every associated feature (e.g. the boat launch apron or beach edge); not adjusted to match the citation since the citation isn't itself a boundary.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Port-owned public open space (OSM operator tag: Port of San Francisco). DataSF's Assessor parcels show active lots at this location without street addresses (for example lot 3941041, added 2019-02-07), so whether the park has its own Assessor lot was not established from a cited source; this feature uses the OSM boundary instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Delivered under the Port of San Francisco's Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan (2010) as the public-open-space component of the Pier 70 area (Port Item 12B, Sept 2018: identified in the 2010 Preferred Master Plan; HPC 2013 packet: a separate project), distinct from and adjacent to Brookfield's 28-acre D4D redevelopment parcel this project's other Pier 70 features are drawn from. Built around a stabilized historic gantry crane and the historic Slipway 4 (Port Resolution 18-61 lists 'stabilization of historic gantry crane (non-functional)'; the crane cabs were eliminated); a human-powered boating center was listed only as a future development opportunity, and Dogpatch Paddle rentals operate from the adjacent YMCA building (Port park page).
properties.notes: Added 2026-09-17 after a user question about whether this map covers the full Pier 70 master plan surfaced that Figure 6.4.2 does not include Crane Cove Park; the figure covers the Pier 70 Special Use District (the 28-Acre Site plus Parcels K North and K South and the Hoedown Yard, about 35 acres per Port Item 11A), not the whole Pier 70 area.
